packs.title: Metal, Trees and Monuments
packs.promise: Find silver panels, tree-path moments and oversized forms beyond the central walk.

q.s: Collect three changes across a silver surface.
st: Find a silver DDP exterior from a public stopping place, or use one of the tourism organization’s exterior photographs.
Collect three visible changes: a panel edge, a curved outline and a lighter or darker patch. Describe what is visible rather than expecting a particular light show.
Arrange the three discoveries from straightest to most curved. Draw or write the order and explain one choice.

q.s: Collect three signs of movement in a still sculpture.
st: Study the horse-and-rider group from an open public path, or use the municipal Horse Statue photograph.
Collect three shapes that suggest movement: choose from a leg, a rider’s lean, a mane, or a line through two figures. No touching or imitation beside the sculpture is needed.
Rank your discoveries from quietest to most energetic. Save your order and the shape that convinced you.

q.s: Build a two-frame picture from a pond-side view.
st: Choose a pond-side view, or study the municipal Mirror Lake photograph. Find one near shape and one shape farther away.
Make two original drawings or two short descriptions: in the first, let the near shape take the lead; in the second, let the far shape lead. A reflection is optional.
Give the two frames different titles. If the pond is dry or closed, use a public tree view or the official photograph for the same near-and-far experiment.

packs.title: Rooflines and Ripples
packs.promise: Find a little Seoul story between a painted eave and a changing reflection.

q.s: Collect a small material portrait of a very wide space.
st: Find a roomy place to stop on a public path beside the lawn and planting in the northern part of the square.
Look for three contrasting textures: a regular paving pattern, an irregular natural surface and a smooth edge. Observe them without touching.
Give each texture a word of its own. Then find one shape that appears in two of your choices.
Save the three textures and the small resemblance that connects them.

q.s: Join a stone curve and a roofline in one tiny caption.
st: Choose a comfortable public viewpoint facing the palace gate, outside queues and access barriers.
Pick one stone arch and one edge of the timber gatehouse roof. Look for the different way each line meets the sky or the wall.
Write exactly six words connecting those two lines. Try a second version by changing one word.
Save the version you prefer and name the two shapes behind it.

q.s: Let a colour, a shape and a small object start a scene.
st: Stop clear of shop doors and the walking route, with a view of a small part of the street.
Choose three ingredients: a colour on a façade, a roof or window shape, and a small object visible from the pavement.
Write a three-sentence imagined scene using those details. Give the small object a role, such as waiting, travelling or being found.
Save the scene with the three details that inspired it.
